text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele and leaders of the governing political parties signed an agreement on cooperation between the parties, aimed at stengthening the government and improving its work work. The pact takes the place of a formal coalition agreement although it has much the same effect.

- The board of the Democratic Party Saimnieks accepted the resignation of parliament speaker and leading member Ilga Kreituse. Kreituse said she was leaving because of the "dictatorship" of leader Ziedonis Chevers. Chevers has also initiated the dismissal of Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss.

- Latvian General Prosecutor Janis Skrastinsh met with Ilga Kreituse to discuss the possibility of bringing a criminal action against deputy Valdis Krisbergs, a member of the Democratic Party Saimnieks.
- Latvian Christian Democrats Union deputy Maris Vitols and the working group including representatives from the Home Guard supported the introduction of military training at universities.

- Most of the governing factions believe that Minister of Finance Kreituss, expelled from his party, will stand down. They also say new candidates for the post will be proposed after the budget has been passed by parliament.
- Two women stole $800,000 from Zemes Bank.
- A seminar on fighting money laundering will take place on September 20 with the participation of the U.S. embassy, the Association of Latvian Commercial Banks and the U.N. Drug Control Programme.

- The Ave Lat company, which controls some 60 percent of the stock exchange quoted Kaija fish cannery, is planning to issue new shares in Kaija although the size of the issue has not been decided yet.
- The government has approved next year's budget draft, which has been drawn up without a deficit.
- The chancellor and deans of departments of the Latvian University are sceptical about the reforms of the univeristy proposed by state minister for higher education Peteris Cimdins.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius announced he is ready to meet Shkele at any time. He pointed out that Lithuania is waiting for Latvia's reply to proposals put forward at the last round of negotiations, a statement which surprised Latvian authorities, who have been looking forward to receive Lithuania's reply.

- A decision next week by European transport ministers could be important for Latvia as they set about approving the 10th multimodal corridor, which include Ventspils port as part of a corridor between western Europe and Russia. Latvia has so far been mentioned only in the corridor from Finland to Poland and western Europe along the Via Baltica.
